title: Core Checkout & Order State Logic

business_context.problem: Lack of explicit business rules for inventory deduction, order state transitions, B2B pricing, and coupon stacking.
business_context.outcome: A clear, testable set of business rules that engineering can implement without ambiguity.
business_context.changed_behavior: Strict rules applied to inventory soft-locks, coupon limits, and failure states.

business_rules: INVENTORY_01: Inventory soft-locks (`inventory_reservations`) are created when a user initiates checkout and expire exactly 15 minutes later.
INVENTORY_02: Inventory is PERMANENTLY deducted from `products.stock_quantity` ONLY when the payment transaction is successful.
ORDER_01: An order is created in `pending_payment` state. If payment fails, it remains `pending_payment` but the inventory soft-lock will expire naturally after 15 mins.
ORDER_02: A background cron job must mark any `pending_payment` order as `abandoned` after 24 hours.
B2B_01: B2B customers pay standard retail/sale prices. No wholesale discounts are applied automatically. The VAT/Company info is strictly for tax invoicing.
COUPON_01: Strict Limit - Only ONE (1) coupon code can be applied per order. If a user enters a new coupon, it replaces the existing one.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user starts checkout, When they proceed to payment, Then a 15-minute soft-lock is placed on the inventory.
Given an active soft-lock, When the payment is successful, Then the product stock is permanently deducted and the lock is removed.
Given an active soft-lock, When the payment fails, Then the order stays `pending_payment` and the user can try again within the 15-minute window.
Given a `pending_payment` order older than 24 hours, When the cron job runs, Then the order status is updated to `abandoned`.
Given a cart with an existing coupon, When the user applies a new valid coupon, Then the old coupon is removed and the new one's discount is applied.
edge_cases: Race Condition: User A's soft-lock expires, User B buys the last item, User A tries to pay. System must reject User A's payment attempt and notify them of out-of-stock.

Stripe Webhook Delay: If the webhook arrives after the soft-lock expires but the payment was actually captured, the system must forcefully deduct inventory (potentially going negative) and alert an admin, OR refund the payment automatically if oversold.
